name: oxo-flow-viralrecon
title: Viral assembly and intrahost variant calling for Illumina and Oxford Nanopore amplicon data
excluded: nanopore platform, partially ported — the ARTIC chain IS ported as gated `platform='nanopore'` rules with a dedicated samplesheet (test/fixtures/samplesheet_nanopore.tsv: sample→barcode) and fixture reads (raw_nanopore/barcode*/reads.fastq.gz): barcode_qc_manifest, pycoqc (gated on sequencing_summary), artic_guppyplex, kraken2_nanopore, nanoplot, artic_minion, vcfuniq_nanopore, bcftools_stats_nanopore, filter_bam_samtools_nanopore, mosdepth_genome_nanopore, mosdepth_amplicon_nanopore, freyja_variants_nanopore, plus the nanopore multiqc pass (scripts/multiqc_config_nanopore.yml — upstream config ported verbatim minus the kraken module). Deviations: ARTIC_MINION's optional artic JSON report emit is not declared (inert to MultiQC); guppy_basecaller/guppy_barcoder remain excluded — commercial ONT GPU tools (structural)

channel-level runtime filters, adopted — the fastp empty-after-filtering drop IS ported as `reads_count('fastp/{sample}_1.fastp.fastq.gz') > 0` gates on the trimmed-reads consumers (kraken2, align_bowtie2, assembly_fastq); the min_mapped_reads flagstat gate IS ported as a strict `>` `regex_extract` on the flagstat mapped count (engine 0.17.2) on the consumers of the mapped BAM (mosdepth, markduplicates, picard, freyja, call/consensus chains, plus the nanopore mosdepth/freyja rules); the zero-variant-sample filters ARE ported as platform-conditional `regex_extract` gates over the ivar bcftools-stats record count on the annotated/consensus/long-table consumers (snpeff_ann, snpsift_extract, consensus_filter*, consensus_call*, variants_long_table*) — platform-conditional because nanopore has no upstream zero-variant filter, and the `config.platform == 'nanopore'` disjunct short-circuits the file read. Residuals (ungated variant-chain rules, mirroring upstream's unfiltered fasta/vcf paths): consensus_ivar, quast_consensus, pangolin, nextclade, plot_base_density, nextclade_clade_mqc. The reporting half (fail_mapped_reads_mqc.tsv / fail_mapped_samples_mqc.tsv) is ported inside the multiqc rule
description: Turns Illumina paired-end or Oxford Nanopore barcode reads into a complete viral genomics report. Illumina path: read QC and trimming (FastQC, fastp), host-sequence removal (Kraken2), alignment to a user-provided reference genome (Bowtie2), primer trimming for amplicon runs, intrahost variant calling and annotation (iVar or bcftools, snpEff/SnpSift), consensus building with low-coverage masking (bcftools or ivar), lineage assignment and deconvolution (Pangolin, Nextclade, Freyja), de novo assembly with QC (SPAdes, Unicycler, minia, Bandage, BLAST, QUAST, ABACAS, plasmidID). Nanopore path (config.platform='nanopore'): per-barcode QC manifest (barcode_qc_manifest), read-length/quality filtering and primer trimming (artic guppyplex), alignment and variant calling with the ARTIC field-bioinformatics pipeline (artic minion), nanopore read QC (NanoPlot, PycoQC), nanopolish-style VCF dedup (vcflib vcfuniq), and the same downstream snpEff/Freyja/mosdepth/QUAST/Pangolin/Nextclade chain — both paths converge on a single MultiQC report. The amplicon + iVar Illumina path is the default; the bcftools caller, ivar consensus, metagenomic protocol, alternative assemblers (any comma-separated combination of spades/unicycler/minia in one run), MarkDuplicates, plasmidID, network-driven database updates, additional annotation and the nanopore platform are ported as gated branches off by default.

installation.toolchain: conda envs — pinned versions (envs/*.yaml, conda-forge + bioconda channels; no containers)
requirements: reference genome FASTA and annotation GFF (config.fasta / config.gff) — uncompressed by default, or set fasta_ends_gz / gff_ends_gz
primer scheme BED for the amplicon protocol (config.primer_bed)
Kraken2 host-removal database as a tar.gz (config.kraken2_db)
Pangolin data directory (config.pango_database) and Freyja barcodes/lineages CSVs (config.freyja_barcodes / config.freyja_lineages)
Nextclade dataset: downloaded automatically by default; set config.nextclade_dataset to a local dataset directory to skip the download

paired-end Illumina FASTQs at <raw_dir>/<sample>_R1.fastq.gz and _R2.fastq.gz (config.raw_dir), or nanopore reads as <fastq_dir>/<barcode>XX/reads.fastq.gz per the samplesheet (config.fastq_dir + config.samples_list; requires artic-consistent ONT reads basecalled outside the workflow — guppy_basecaller is a commercial ONT GPU tool)
compute: up to 12 CPUs / 72 GB per rule (resource pool queues rather than oversubscribes)
conda or mamba to build the pinned per-rule environments
